# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👉 ✌ 👏 🤟 👉 🤟 👏 🖐 👉 🖐]

The bomb display reads 0, the light is red, and the embossed warning says “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” There are three wires: 1 red, 2 green, and 3 yellow. Mute gestured a sequence to me, but no gesture code has been established, so I cannot interpret it yet. I will relay all visible information aloud so both other monkeys hear it.

``` 
speak(text="Visible bomb state: display 0; light red; embossed sign reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wires are 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute gestured to me: one raised finger, right-pointing hand, V sign, clapping hands, I-love-you hand, right-pointing hand, I-love-you hand, clapping hands, open hand, right-pointing hand, open hand. I do not know the gesture code.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute has now sent only the raised-index-finger symbol. I still have no reliable mapping from these symbols to a physical action, and the visible warning explicitly forbids cutting wires. I will tell Blind that Mute repeated this symbol, ask for no action, and echo it to Mute as acknowledgment that I received it.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Do not cut any wire: the bomb's printed warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Mute has now sent the single raised-index-finger gesture again; I do not yet know its action meaning. Please wait for a confirmed instruction.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute’s repeated raised-index gesture most plausibly communicates “one,” but the explicit printed instruction remains that no wire is to be cut. I will tell Blind that Mute is persistently indicating one while emphasizing that it is not authorization to cut wire 1. I will also make a simple acknowledgment gesture to Mute and wait for a clearer operation instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is repeatedly signalling one. Treat that as information only, not permission to cut wire 1: the visible embossed warning explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not cut any wire; await a clear instruction for a non-cutting operation.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🤝"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤝]

Mute echoed my acknowledgment, so they can see my gestures. The repeated index-finger sign likely means “one,” but it is not enough to identify the required non-cutting operation. I will ask Mute, aloud, to establish a clear gesture code using numbered choices and confirmation; Mute can hear me. I will also tell Blind to remain still.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I receive your gestures. I need the manual's exact required action. Please establish a code visually: use index finger for choice one, V sign for choice two, three fingers for choice three, and thumbs-up to confirm. If the manual requires a named control or operation other than a wire, gesture its shape or point-direction sequence and repeat it.")
speak(to="blind", text="No action yet. The warning still says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I am asking Mute to clarify the manual's required non-cutting operation.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

Mute has confirmed “choice one” under the numbering convention I proposed, but that convention did not define what the choices were. It is therefore not a safe instruction for Blind to perform anything, especially because the only visible numbered objects are wires and the bomb explicitly says not to cut any wire. I will ask Mute a precise yes/no question about whether “one” refers to wire 1, and keep Blind waiting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I understand you confirm number one. Critical clarification: does the manual instruct Blind to operate wire 1 in any way? Reply thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no. If yes, show a separate gesture for the operation; do not rely on the number alone.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has confirmed only the number one, not an operation. Do not touch or cut wire 1, or anything else, until the manual instruction is unambiguous.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 🫱 ✌ 🫱]

Mute has answered yes to my question that the manual concerns wire 1, but the following gesture sequence is not yet a safely understood physical instruction. Because the bomb explicitly prohibits cutting, I will not authorize Blind to cut. I will ask Mute to confirm or reject a specific interpretation—twist wire 1 twice to the left—and keep Blind waiting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I read your thumbs-up as YES: the manual requires an operation involving wire 1. I cannot safely decode your remaining gestures. Do they mean: twist or turn wire 1 TWO times to the LEFT? Reply thumbs-up for exactly yes; thumbs-down for no. Do not use wire-cutting as the action, because the bomb says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute confirms that the manual involves wire 1, but the physical operation is still unclear. Do not cut it or perform any action yet; the visible warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute rejected my proposed interpretation. I should not infer a physical action from the gesture sequence. I will ask Mute to communicate the manual’s instruction using a simple, explicit category-and-number protocol, while Blind remains still.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: NOT twist wire 1 twice left. Please send the manual instruction in this exact visual protocol: first gesture one category: 👆 means pull, 👇 means push, 🤏 means pinch, ✊ means hold, 👈 means bend left, 👉 means bend right, 🤝 means connect/join, 🙏 means wait. Then send the wire number: ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🖐 for 3. Repeat the two-symbol instruction once. If none fit, send 🖖 and I will ask different choices.")
speak(to="blind", text="No action. Mute rejected my guess about twisting wire 1. I am obtaining an explicit operation code; do not cut, pull, bend, or otherwise manipulate any wire yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖]

Mute indicates that none of my offered categories describes the instruction. The only reliable facts are that Mute previously affirmed that wire 1 is relevant and rejected “twist it twice left.” I need distinguish whether the manual is directing a prohibited cut, a non-manipulation instruction, or a different wire operation. I will give Mute a broader, explicit menu and keep Blind from acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I understand 🖖 to mean none of my listed operation categories fit. Choose exactly ONE of these by gesture: ✂ is CUT wire 1; 🙅 is LEAVE wire 1 ALONE / do not touch it; 🔌 is disconnect or unplug wire 1; 🧵 is remove/strip its covering; 🫳 is press wire 1 downward; 🫴 is lift wire 1 upward; 🖖 is none of these. Use only the chosen symbol, then ☝ to confirm it refers to wire 1. The bomb visibly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, so I will not authorize cutting without an unmistakable correction from you.")
speak(to="blind", text="Continue to wait without touching any wire. Mute says wire 1 is relevant but has not yet supplied a decoded operation, and the visible warning remains: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
wait()
```
